text:
samir: Hey team — running into weird Key Vault behavior when using a managed identity from our app in subscription A to access a vault in subscription B/tenant. Getting 403 with 'Identity not found' after a rotation. Anyone seen cross-tenant MSI issues?
amelia: Are you on Azure RBAC for the vault or using access policies? RBAC role assignments are tenant-scoped which matters for cross-tenant identities.
samir: It's an AKS pod using aad-pod-identity (user-assigned MI). Vault is set to 'Azure RBAC' (not Access Policies).
jordan: If you're using RBAC, the managed identity needs a role assignment scoped to the vault (or resource group/subscription). Role assignments are recorded in the tenant where the identity is defined. Cross-tenant direct MSI calls are usually unsupported; you need a service principal or guest identity in the target tenant.
amelia: Also confirm the AAD access token audience — it must be for resource https://vault.azure.net. If your token is for management.azure.com or something else, vault will reject with 403.
samir: Paste of the error: 
```
StatusCode: 403
Code: Forbidden
Message: Identity '6f4a2c9e-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxx' was not found in this vault's tenant
```
olivia: For rotation context: if you're using envelope encryption (CEK/DEK model), rotating the KEK (Key Vault key) requires rewrapping DEKs or relying on key versioning. If you rotate the KEK and don't rewrap existing DEKs, older ciphertexts will fail to unwrap.
samir: We're running an automated rotation job that creates a new key version and expects unwrap to keep working. Do we need to run wrapKey for every DEK to re-encrypt with the new key version?
olivia: Typically yes. Pattern: 1) Create new key version. 2) For each stored DEK ciphertext, call unwrapKey with old key version then wrapKey with new key version (or call wrapKey on the plaintext DEK). If you can't rewrap immediately, keep old key versions available so unwrapKey still works.
jordan: Permission nuance: Azure RBAC requires roles that grant cryptography operations (e.g., Key Vault Crypto User or a custom role). Ensure the role includes microsoft.keyvault/vaults/deploy/action? Actually the key actions are microsoft.keyvault/keys/* and under RBAC they map to keyActions like wrapKey/unwrapKey. Check that the assigned role includes keyActions: ["wrapKey","unwrapKey"].
amelia: Also watch object IDs vs principal IDs. A role assignment expects the principal ID from the tenant where the identity lives. If you have a guest SPN, it may have a different object id in the other tenant. Cross-tenant setups often require creating a service principal in the vault's tenant or using a managed identity inside the same tenant.
sec-bot: [alert] 2026-02-12 09:23:10 - Key rotation job failed: rewrap timeout for 3 DEKs. ticket #INC-3212
samir: Okay — that matches: rotation job timed out while trying to unwrap old DEKs. I'll check role assignment scope and token audience, and add retries/backoff to rotation.
olivia: I can share a small script that enumerates keys, lists versions, and safely rewraps DEKs (with checkpointing) if you want. Also add a flag to keep old key versions for 30 days before purge as a safety.
amelia: TL;DR recommendations: 1) Prefer colocating vault/identity in same tenant when possible. 2) If using AZ RBAC, ensure correct role assignment scope and principal id in vault tenant. 3) For rotation, implement rewrap + graceful fallback to old key versions. 4) Confirm token audience is https://vault.azure.net.
samir: Thanks — I'll run a repro with curl to get the raw token and show the roles. Will follow up with logs and the rotation job trace.
olivia: Example wrapKey call snippet we use: 
```bash
# wrap a 256-bit DEK with a specific key version
TOKEN=$(az account get-access-token --resource https://vault.azure.net --query accessToken -o tsv)
curl -s -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"alg":"RSA-OAEP-256","value":"<base64-dek>"}' \ 
  https://my-vault.vault.azure.net/keys/my-key/<key-version>/wrapkey?api-version=7.3
```
samir: Perfect — that should help. I'll ping once I have the trace.
